dispositions.topic_text: Required verification of exact OWNER_AUDIT_ACTIONS table coverage and audit-action values
The concrete confirmation digest construction, including encoding, domain separation, algorithm, strength, and representation
dispositions.what: The confirmation digest's construction: a typed injective encoding of (action, target, version, inputs in the model's field order, lists in their order, absent told apart from empty), with domain separation, under a release-fixed collision-resistant cryptographic digest (e.g. SHA-256) and its text representation. Options: length-prefixed typed binary, canonical CBOR, or another injective encoding. Every option must keep A13 rule 6: two different tuples never share an encoding; only a digest collision is outside the guarantee; the values themselves are never kept.
keeps:
The digest is a collision-resistant cryptographic digest of one
   unambiguous encoding of the action, the target, the version and the inputs
   in that order, every list in its order and an absent value told apart from
   an empty one, so that two different tuples never share an encoding; that
   two encodings share a digest is outside the guarantee.
options: Use a typed length-prefixed binary encoding with explicit field and collection tags, domain separation, and SHA-256.
Use canonical CBOR with fixed schemas and domain separation, hashed with SHA-256.
Use another release-fixed injective typed encoding and an approved collision-resistant digest.
consequences: A custom encoding needs explicit vectors and careful type and length handling; canonical CBOR adds a dependency and requires strict canonical enforcement; another construction must independently establish injectivity and adequate collision resistance.
